name: Canceling the Free Coordinates of a Positioned Cube
statement: Suppose one sign-compatible vector with coordinate magnitudes in $[t,1]$ is given for every word in a positioned cube fixing a partial pattern $q$, where $0<t\le1$. A convex combination of the vectors has zeros on every free cube coordinate and signed magnitudes in $[t,1]$ on the fixed support. It preserves every linear inequality common to the input vectors; rational inputs admit a construction by $2^d-1$ rational pair averages, where $d$ is the cube dimension.
proof: Choose strict witnesses for all cube vertices. Pair vertices opposite in one free coordinate and take a positive convex combination that cancels that coordinate. Fixed signs and all strict linear separator inequalities survive. Repeat over the free coordinates; previously canceled coordinates remain zero.
